Ein interessanter Rückblick auf das ereignisreiche Jahr der nationalen Erhebung in Deutschland, vom 30. Januar 1933 bis jetzt!

Der historische 30. Januar 1933 in Berlin.

  • Poster or postcard with coloured drawings depicting the progression of the German Nazi Party (NSDAP) and the brownshirt uniforms of the Sturmabteilung (SA), the party's paramilitary "street thugs" troops, from the veteran's Freikorps movements after the end of World War I, through the party ban 1923–25, the 1930 uniform ban was lifted by Reich President Paul von Hindenburg in June 1932 to the January 1933 election of Hitler as Chancellor
  • Uniforms and insignia of the Sturmabteilung (SA); Hitler salute; Swastika flag, etc.

ImageDescription.value:
Nazi seizure of power: The staff of the Führer taken on the day of his appointment as Reich Chancellor on January 30, 1933.

From left to right:

  • Oberpräsident Wilhelm Kube
  • Justice Minister Hanns Kerrl
  • Minister Dr. Joseph Goebbels
  • Der Führer Adolf Hitler
  • Chief of Staff Ernst Röhm
  • Ministerpräsident Hermann Göring
  • Minister Walther Darré
  • Reichsführer of the SS Heinrich Himmler
  • Deputy Führer Rudolf Hess
  • Minister Wilhelm Frick seated in the front

pages.title: File:Kundgebung und Fackelzug der Nationalsozialisten am 31. Januar 1933 in Köln.jpg

ObjectName.value: Kundgebung und Fackelzug der Nationalsozialisten am 31. Januar 1933 in Köln

ImageDescription.value:
Kölnische Zeitung February 1, 1933: Assembly and Torchlight Parade in Cologne; Cologne, January 31.
The National Socialists held a rally this evening in the exhibition hall to celebrate Hitler's appointment as Reich Chancellor. The large hall and the adjacent Majolica Hall were so overcrowded long before the event began that they had to be closed by the police. The rally also included several flag delegations from the Stahlhelm organization, which were received with particular applause. After the entry of the flags and several fanfare marches, Gauleiter Grohé (M. d. L.) gave a speech. He said, among other things:
"Yesterday was a decisive day for Germany. The November system has been overthrown, and a new Germany is emerging. Thanks must be given to the renowned Field Marshal and Reich President von Hindenburg for entrusting Hitler with the office of Reich Chancellor. There had often been doubts about whether Hindenburg understood young Germany as well. All the greater, therefore, is the joy at yesterday's decision by the Reich President.
The National Socialists are proud of Hitler because he is a man of action. It fills everyone with satisfaction that all of national Germany has now come together for joint efforts. Not only Germany, but the entire world, has been stirred by Hitler's appointment as Reich Chancellor. The world is listening because it knows that Germany is gaining new life. The National Socialist movement and Hitler's government are firmly determined to use every means of power to combat communism if the interests of the fatherland demand it.
The era of political parties is definitively over. Now there is only one party, and that party is Germany. Hitler has now come to power and will never relinquish that power. Anyone who acts against the interests of the nation will no longer have freedom in Germany.
In conclusion, Grohé emphasized that the National Socialists are firmly committed to following their leader, Hitler, in every way. They are prepared for any effort, knowing that at the end of this struggle, a Germany of honor and freedom must stand."
After Grohé's speech, Stahlhelm leader Haumann gave a brief address urging unity. The assembly sent a telegram of thanks to Hindenburg and a tribute telegram to Hitler.
Following the rally, a torchlight parade took place through the main streets of the city, involving the SA, the SS, the Hitler Youth, and a group from the Stahlhelm. On the Hohenzollernring, a march-past was held in front of the leaders of the Cologne-Aachen Gau.

Credit.value: Kölnische Zeitung 1. Februar 1933
